The BBA'97 home health policy change had a significant impact on home care use among the impaired elderly.
Medicare's 1997 home health policy, the Interim Policy System (IPS) dramatically decreased the use of home health services by Medicare patients with functional, health and memory impairment.
the Balanced Budget Act of1997 dramatically decreased reimbursements for Medicare home health care.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the differential impact of Medicare home health care policy on impaired beneficiaries.
the differential impact of Medicare home health policy on impaired beneficiaries.
the impact of the Balanced Budget Act of1997 (B.B.A. 1997) on the Medicare home health care program.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(1) The BBA 97 IPS policy changes had differential effects on home health use by impaired Medicare beneficiaries, (2) the IPS policy changes were associated with significant decreases in home health care use among beneficiaries with ADL impairments, (3) the IPS policy change was also associated with significant decreases for beneficiaries with memory and health impairments, and (4) the IPS policy was not associated with decreases in use among beneficiaries with no impairments.

the Balanced Budget Act of1997 (B.B.A.) has had a negative impact on the home health care use of the most impaired beneficiaries, and the impact of the B.B.A. has been greatest on the most impaired beneficiaries.
the IPS had an adverse impact on the use of home health services for the most impaired Medicare beneficiaries, but the magnitude of the adverse impact varied with the type of impairment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BBA 1997 had a differential impact on impaired beneficiaries.
home health care is an important source of care for persons with impairments.
the BBA'97 IPS had a negative and differential effect on impaired patients, and that this effect was moderated by race/ethnicity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
policy makers should not assume that a one-size-fits-all policy will have the same impact on different subpopulations.
policy changes in the Medicare home care system may have differential effects on beneficiaries with varying degrees of health and functional impairment.
